**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify the frozen mutation stream before reporting MATCH**

Reconstruct the preregistered mutation stream and verify each policy ID against its parameters rather than checking only that 120 IDs are unique. As written, a producer defect can substitute any unique ID or out-of-range policy for a cut mutant and update the corresponding rows, panels, and policy map; the recompute still prints `MATCH` because all later calculations trust the self-reported manifest. This leaves the frozen mutation seed and gene ranges independently unverified even though this script supports the ledger evidence.

AGENTS.md reference: [solver/AGENTS.md:L3-L8](https://github.com/eluckey2002/Map-Elites-2248/blob/e8d9ef1daa4e8b69478c62db941b2c4ac7b43876/solver/AGENTS.md#L3-L8)

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Count actual fresh refusals instead of archive compression**

When multiple nominees share a cell and a later fresh-admitted nominee replaces an earlier admitted nominee, `nominees.length - finalArchive.size` reports one refusal even though neither nominee failed the fresh admission rule. This makes the protocol-required `recheck_refused` headline conflate rejected candidates with successful same-cell replacements; increment a refusal counter from each `admit()` result instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make the qualification fixture consumable by recompute**

The generated qualification artifact cannot exercise the independent recompute it is intended to qualify: this panel list omits `bad72` and all winner-curse panels, while `recompute.js` unconditionally aggregates them. Running `node solver/ruler/recompute.js docs/goals/trustworthy-ruler/recompute-qualification.json` therefore crashes at the missing `bad72` candidate panel before reaching the MAP checks, so the committed fixture provides no executable qualification coverage.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce the preregistered size of every panel**

Validate `panel.games` and the retained row count against `panel.levels.length * panel.seeds.length`, not only against each other. For example, truncating the stage-2 candidate from 600 to 599 rows and changing both self-reported counts to 599 still makes this recompute exit successfully with `MATCH`, even though the protocol makes a missing raw pair invalid and fixes that stage at 600 games. Thus an incomplete experiment can be independently certified as complete.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve negative infinity for zero-variance regressions**

When every mutual-win cell has the same negative move difference, the mean is negative and `moveSe` is zero, but this branch sets the statistic to zero and reports `t='0.000000'`. The registered statistic is mean divided by SE, so this case should report negative infinity; the current output masks a perfectly consistent regression even though the stronger-policy verdict remains false.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retain the preregistered win-axis uncertainty**

Include `winRateDifference`, the level/seed win SEs, the selected win SE, and `winCi95` in the retained summary and printed evidence. `summarizePairs()` computes these values, but `compact()` keeps only win counts before switching to move uncertainty, so every stored headline and report omits the win-axis SE and 95% interval that the protocol explicitly requires for each paired comparison; the independent recompute consequently cannot confirm that declared output either.
